6º de Primaria · Inglés

Jobs, hobbies and free time

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si alguien te pregunta «What do you do in your free time?», ¿te está preguntando por tu trabajo o por tus aficiones?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Por tus aficiones: «in your free time» significa «en tu tiempo libre». Contestarías «I play the drums» o «I love reading». Para preguntar por el trabajo se dice What do you do? o What's your job?: «I'm a nurse».

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: The last lighthouse keeper

My great-grandfather Tomás was a lighthouse keeper. He lived with his family in a small white house next to a lighthouse on the coast of Galicia.

Every evening, when the sun went down, he climbed the 120 steps to the top of the tower and switched on the light. All night, he had to check that the light was working, because ships needed it to avoid the dangerous rocks. When there was fog, he turned on the foghorn. In the morning, he cleaned the big glass lens until it was shining.

It was a lonely job, but he loved it. In his free time, he was keen on fishing and painting. He was very good at painting boats, and he was proud of his pictures of the sea. My grandmother still has them in her living room.

Today, most lighthouses work automatically, and there are almost no lighthouse keepers. Some jobs disappear and new jobs appear. Maybe one day my job will disappear too! But I hope people will always need stories, because I want to be a writer.

1. Jobs

Here are some common jobs: a doctor, a nurse (enfermero/a), a teacher, a firefighter (bombero/a), a police officer, a vet (veterinario/a), a farmer, a chef (cocinero/a), a mechanic, an engineer, a journalist, a pilot, a shop assistant (dependiente) and a scientist.

In English we use a / an before a job: «She's a pilot», «He's an engineer». En castellano: decimos «es piloto» sin artículo, pero en inglés el a es obligatorio. Muchos trabajos sirven para hombres y mujeres: firefighter, police officer.

2. Job words: -er, -or, -ist, -ian

Many job words in English are made with a suffix at the end of a verb or a noun. Knowing these suffixes helps you to understand and spell new words:

  • -er (the most common): teach → teacher, farm → farmer, build → builder, bake → baker, paint → painter, write → writer, design → designer, programme → programmer.
  • -or: act → actor, direct → director, invent → inventor, sail → sailor, doctor.
  • -ist: art → artist, science → scientist, journal → journalist, dentist, pianist, cyclist.
  • -ian: music → musician, electric → electrician, library → librarian, politician.

Some jobs have special words: chef (from French), pilot, nurse, firefighter, police officer, vet (short for veterinarian).

Notice that in English most job words are the same for men and women: a teacher, a doctor, an engineer. Today we usually say firefighter instead of fireman, and police officer instead of policeman.

3. Where do they work? What do they do?

To ask about a job: «What does your mum do?» – «She's a vet». To say where: «She works in an animal hospital». We say works in a hospital / an office / a shop / a school, works on a farm and works at home / the airport.

To explain the job, use the present simple: «A firefighter puts out fires and rescues people», «A chef cooks food in a restaurant», «A journalist writes news». En castellano: recuerda la -s de la tercera persona.

4. Jobs of the past and the future

The world of work is always changing. Some jobs have almost disappeared because of new technology:

  • Lighthouse keepers: today lighthouses work automatically.
  • Switchboard operators: they connected telephone calls by hand.
  • Milkmen: they brought fresh milk to people's doors every morning.
  • Typists: they wrote documents on typewriters.

And many new jobs have appeared in the last few years, and more will appear in the future. Some experts think these jobs will be important:

  • App developers and video game designers, who create programs for computers and phones.
  • Drone pilots, who use drones to take photos, deliver packages or check fields and forests.
  • Renewable energy technicians, who install and repair solar panels and wind turbines.
  • Data scientists, who study huge amounts of information to find answers.
  • Carers for elderly people, because people live longer.

Nobody knows exactly what jobs will exist when you grow up. That's why it's important to keep learning, be creative and be good at working in a team.

Vídeo: 100 Kids Tell Us What They Want to Be When They Grow Up | 100 Kids | HiHo Kids · HiHo Kids (YouTube) · 4,5 millones de visualizaciones

5. Hobbies and free time

Hobbies are activities we do for fun in our free time. Some go with play: play football, play chess, play the guitar, play video games. Some go with go + -ing: go swimming, go skating, go cycling, go hiking, go shopping. Some go with do: do karate, do gymnastics, do yoga, do puzzles.

Others: read comics, draw, paint, dance, sing in a choir, cook, take photos, collect stickers. En castellano: fíjate en que con los instrumentos se dice play the: «play the piano».

6. Likes and dislikes + -ing

After like, love, enjoy, don't mind and hate we use the verb with -ing: «I love dancing», «She enjoys reading», «I don't mind cleaning my room», «He hates getting up early».

From most to least: love → really like → like → don't mind (no me importa) → don't like → hate. Questions: «Do you like cooking?» – «Yes, I do!». En castellano: «me gusta bailar» se dice «I like dancing», con -ing, no «I like dance».

Vídeo: Hobbies and interests: what do you like doing? · English Singsing (YouTube) · 4,7 millones de visualizaciones

7. Good at, interested in

To talk about skills we say be good at + noun or -ing: «I'm good at drawing», «She's good at Maths», «I'm not very good at singing». To talk about interests: be interested in: «He's interested in space and planets».

Other useful expressions: be into (estar enganchado a): «I'm really into manga», and be a fan of: «I'm a big fan of basketball». En castellano: «se me da bien dibujar» = «I'm good at drawing».

8. Keen on, proud of, afraid of

Many adjectives in English go with a particular preposition. You have to learn them together, because they are often different from Spanish:

  • keen on (very interested in): «I'm keen on photography.»
  • fond of (likes a lot): «My grandpa is fond of gardening.»
  • crazy about (loves): «She's crazy about horses.»
  • proud of (orgulloso de): «I'm proud of my drawings.»
  • afraid of / scared of (tener miedo de): «He's afraid of spiders.»
  • bored with (aburrido de): «I'm bored with this game.»
  • tired of (harto de): «I'm tired of waiting.»
  • bad at (malo en): «I'm bad at singing.»
  • worried about (preocupado por): «Mum's worried about the exam.»

Remember: after a preposition, a verb takes -ing: «I'm keen on dancing.» «She's afraid of flying.» «I'm tired of doing homework.»

Notice the difference with Spanish: «estoy orgulloso de» is «proud of», but «bueno en» is «good at».

Vídeo: Adjectives and Prepositions | Learn British English with Lucy | · English with Lucy (YouTube) · 822 mil visualizaciones

9. How often?

To ask how often (con qué frecuencia) we say How often do you…? «How often do you go swimming?» – «Twice a week». Answers: every day, once a week (una vez a la semana), twice a month, three times a year, at the weekend, on Mondays.

Or use frequency adverbs: always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever, never. «I usually play tennis on Saturdays», «I hardly ever watch TV» (casi nunca).

10. When I grow up…

To talk about the future job we say I want to be… or I'd like to be… + a / an: «I want to be a marine biologist», «I'd like to be an architect». Give a reason with because: «...because I love animals and the sea».

Connect hobbies and jobs: «I'm good at drawing, so I'd like to be a designer». «I enjoy helping people, so I want to be a nurse». En castellano: «When I grow up» significa «cuando sea mayor».

11. Reading: a survey

Read the results of a class survey (encuesta): «In our class, 25 students answered. Football is the most popular hobby: nine students play it every week. Video games are second: eight students play them, but most only at the weekend. Six students love reading and five do dance classes. Four students are really good at drawing. When they grow up, three students want to be vets, two want to be teachers and one wants to be an astronaut!»

12. Let's practise: find someone who…

Walk around the class and ask questions. Find someone who: can play an instrument, is good at cooking, goes hiking at the weekend, hates getting up early, wants to be a scientist. Ask: «Do you go hiking?», «Are you good at cooking?».

Then write a short profile of a classmate: «Marta is eleven. In her free time she loves skating and she goes swimming twice a week. She's good at Science and she wants to be an engineer».

13. A job interview

When people apply for a job, they usually have a job interview. The interviewer asks questions to find out if the person is right for the job. Imagine you want to be a volunteer at the town library this summer. Here are some typical questions and answers:

  • «Can you tell me something about yourself?» – «I'm eleven years old and I'm in Year 6. I'm very keen on reading.»
  • «Why do you want this job?» – «Because I love books and I'd like to help younger children to enjoy reading.»
  • «What are you good at?» – «I'm good at organising things and I'm very patient.»
  • «What are you bad at?» – «Sometimes I'm a bit shy, but I'm trying to improve.»
  • «Can you work in a team?» – «Yes, I can. I often do group projects at school.»
  • «Do you have any questions?» – «Yes. What time do I have to start?»

Tips for a good interview: be on time, smile, look at the interviewer, listen carefully, answer with full sentences and give examples. At the end, say «Thank you for your time».

14. Volunteering

A volunteer is a person who works without a salary to help other people, animals or the environment. Millions of people around the world volunteer in their free time. Here are some examples:

  • Helping at an animal shelter: feeding dogs and cats, walking them and cleaning their cages.
  • Collecting food for a food bank, which gives food to families who need it.
  • Cleaning beaches, rivers and forests.
  • Visiting elderly people who live alone, reading to them or playing games with them.
  • Helping younger children with their homework.
  • Working with the Red Cross or other organisations when there are emergencies.

Why do people volunteer? Because it makes them feel useful and happy, they meet new people and they learn new skills. Many people say that they receive more than they give.

Children can volunteer too, with their families or their school: a charity sale, a toy collection at Christmas or a clean-up day in the park. What could your class do to help your community?

In many countries there is an International Volunteer Day on 5th December. On that day, organisations thank their volunteers and invite new people to join them. Some schools organise a volunteering week with activities like collecting books for a library, making cards for a hospital or planting trees in the playground. Small actions can make a big difference!

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Answer: «What does a vet do?»

  1. Presente simple, tercera persona con -s.
  2. Explica la tarea principal.

Resultado: A vet looks after sick animals.

Ejemplo 2. Complete: «I love (play) ___ the drums.»

  1. Después de love → -ing.
  2. play the + instrumento.

Resultado: I love playing the drums.

Ejemplo 3. Choose play, go or do: «___ karate», «___ skating», «___ chess».

  1. Artes marciales → do.
  2. Actividad en -ing → go.
  3. Juego de reglas → play.

Resultado: do karate, go skating, play chess.

Ejemplo 4. Form the job: science, music, act.

  1. science → -ist.
  2. music → -ian.
  3. act → -or.

Resultado: scientist, musician, actor.

Ejemplo 5. Complete: «I'm afraid ___ (fly).»

  1. afraid goes with of.
  2. After a preposition, -ing.

Resultado: I'm afraid of flying.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el artículo: «She's teacher» → «She's a teacher».
  • Usar el infinitivo tras like: «I like swim» → «I like swimming».
  • Olvidar the con instrumentos: «I play guitar» → «I play the guitar».
  • Confundir play y go: «play swimming» → «go swimming».
  • Preposición incorrecta: «good in Maths» → «good at Maths».
  • Decir «I'm good in maths»: se dice good at.
  • Poner el verbo sin -ing tras preposición: «keen on dance» en lugar de «keen on dancing».

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Write the job: «This person helps sick animals.»

    Ver solución
    a vet.

  2. Write the job: «This person puts out fires.»

    Ver solución
    a firefighter.

  3. Complete with in, on or at: «A farmer works ___ a farm.»

    Ver solución
    on.

  4. Form job words: farm, invent, art, library.

    Ver solución
    farmer, inventor, artist, librarian.

  5. Complete: «I'm proud ___ my sister.»

    Ver solución
    of.

  6. What did a lighthouse keeper do?

    Ver solución
    He switched on and checked the light so ships could avoid the rocks.

  7. What is a volunteer?

    Ver solución
    A person who works without a salary to help others.

  8. Name a job of the future.

    Ver solución
    Drone pilot (app developer, data scientist…).

Nivel medio

  1. Complete with play, go or do: «___ yoga», «___ hiking», «___ the piano».

    Ver solución
    do yoga, go hiking, play the piano.

  2. Complete: «She enjoys (read) ___ comics.»

    Ver solución
    reading.

  3. Correct: «I'm good in drawing.»

    Ver solución
    I'm good at drawing.

  4. Answer: «How often do you brush your teeth?»

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Three times a day.

  5. Translate: «Cuando sea mayor quiero ser arquitecta.»

    Ver solución
    When I grow up I want to be an architect.

  6. Complete with the right preposition: keen ___, bored ___, worried ___.

    Ver solución
    on, with, about.

  7. Write two sentences: something you are keen on and something you are afraid of.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  8. Why are some jobs disappearing?

    Ver solución
    Because of new technology (machines do them automatically).

  9. Answer the interview question: «What are you good at?»

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: I'm good at drawing and working in a team.

  10. Why do people volunteer?

    Ver solución
    They feel useful and happy, meet people and learn new skills.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Write two hobbies you like and one you don't like.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I love dancing and I like cooking. I don't like running.

  2. Write a short profile of a family member (job and hobbies).

    Ver solución
    Model answer: My uncle is a mechanic. He works in a garage. In his free time he goes cycling.

  3. Write five interview questions and answers for a summer job at a zoo.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Describe a job you think will exist in 2050 and explain what the person will do.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Plan a volunteering project for your class (what, where, when, who).

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Interview an older person about a job that doesn't exist now.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeJobs fair

La clase organiza una feria de oficios en inglés con profesiones del pasado, del presente y del futuro.

Pasos

  1. Cada pareja elige una profesión e investiga qué hace, dónde trabaja y qué habilidades necesita.
  2. Preparad un póster con el nombre del oficio, su sufijo y frases con good at y keen on.
  3. Ensayad una entrevista de trabajo para esa profesión.
  4. Celebrad la feria y proponed un proyecto de voluntariado para la clase.

Producto final: Una feria de oficios con pósteres, entrevistas y un proyecto de voluntariado.

Cómo se valora

  • Forms job words with suffixes.
  • Uses adjectives with prepositions and -ing.
  • Asks and answers interview questions.
  • Shows interest in helping the community.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Entrevistad en inglés a un familiar sobre su trabajo: «What do you do? Where do you work?».
  • Haced juntos una lista de aficiones de la familia con play, go y do.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Profesiones, aficiones y tiempo libre; gustos con verbos + -ing; frecuencia; planes de futuro (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Encuesta de aficiones de la clase con gráfico de barras.
  • Juego «Find someone who…».
  • Juego de mímica de profesiones con What do I do?

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn vocabulary for jobs and workplaces
  • Talk about hobbies with like / love / enjoy + -ing
  • Ask and answer about free time and how often
  • Talk about what you want to be in the future
  • Form job words with -er, -or, -ist and -ian
  • Talk about jobs of the past and of the future
  • Use adjectives with prepositions: keen on, proud of, afraid of
  • Prepare a job interview and learn about volunteering

Palabras clave

jobs · What does she do? · works in / at · hobbies · free time · like / love / hate + -ing · be good at · How often…? · want to be

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
